title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate
audience: Any home-service operator, including solo operators, starting or growing a business.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: "I will clean your house" is a service. "I will leave your kitchen and bathrooms ready for guests within 3 hours, or I will redo the rooms that fail the checklist at no charge" is an offer. The customer buys the result and the certainty of getting it.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome; a defined time frame; the work the customer must do; the certainty you provide (checklists, photos, guarantee); and the risk you carry. Keep each part specific and checkable. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make the booking, access and handover simple. Fewer steps and fewer decisions for the customer usually allow a higher price, because the customer is paying for convenience and reliability.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and are able to pay for. In Australia, consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services, and they cannot be removed by contract. Claims about results, including any measured percentage improvement, must be substantiated. Check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measurable claim. A written workmanship warranty is an optional extra that sits on top of the consumer guarantees rather than replacing them, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025).

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, then check against your cost and time. A premium rate is justified when the customer can see the result, the certainty and the saved time. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin, so check the price against cost before deciding on any premium (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025). Stepped packages, with each higher level adding something the customer can see, are one way to present the offer (Jobber Academy, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). Show one clear total and say whether GST is included; Western Australia's consumer agency guidance asks for this (WA Consumer Protection, updated 4 September 2026).

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a customer would repeat.
Set a time frame you have checked against your past jobs, and record how often you meet it.
List what the customer must do and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element (checklist, photos, sign-off).
Decide the guarantee and check that you can afford it.
Price from value, then check the rate against cost and time.

workedExamples.situation: A gardener quotes an hourly rate and loses jobs to cheaper quotes. Customers say they cannot tell what they will get.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer and price it.
workedExamples.reasoning: A fixed-scope package with a photo checklist and a return visit for missed items gives the customer certainty, which supports a higher package price than an hourly quote.

commonErrors.error: Making a guarantee you cannot afford to honour
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the guarantee to something you control, such as a return visit.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have measured and can show.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: A good offer promises an outcome with a time frame, certainty and a fair guarantee.
Higher rates follow from clearer value, not from longer hours.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of an offer does the customer buy?
What should a guarantee be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a measurable claim such as a percentage improvement have?

officialReferences.title: Advertising and selling guide: A guide for business (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: Guide dated July 2021; the text read covers the first 100,000 of about 123,600 characters. States that services are guaranteed to be provided with due care and skill, to be fit for any purpose specified by the consumer, and to be provided within a reasonable time where no time is agreed; consumer guarantees cannot be excluded by contract. States that premium claims must be substantiated, and that credence claims are those the consumer cannot independently verify. Publisher: ACCC.

sourceReferences: Solopreneur Start-Up Guide, Step 3 (Tom Scourfield; distribution rights held by the user). Adapted for home-service operators; sales pitch at the end of the guide omitted.
localised to Australian practice; no rate or percentage is stated in this lesson unless a source states it.
